{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793095632000,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01KRhKuSipBD83gwVTdcikMo","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA sparse matrix-vector multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI: rows are partitioned across ranks, balanced by non-zero count.\n//          Each rank owns a contiguous block of CSR rows. The matrix is\n//          generated deterministically on every rank (identical to the serial\n//          generator), so no matrix data is communicated. The dense vector is\n//          constant across iterations, so the timed loop needs no communication.\n//   - CUDA: each rank drives one GPU (selected by node-local rank) and runs a\n//          CSR kernel with one thread per row. Each row is summed in the same\n//          left-to-right order as the reference CPU code.\n//   - OpenMP: host-side work that is data-parallel and rank-local: slicing the\n//          CSR data for the rank's rows, and the CPU reference SpMV used for\n//          validation. The random matrix generator is inherently sequential\n//          (it consumes one rand() stream) and is kept serial so the generated\n//          matrix is identical to the original program.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdarg>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\nconstexpr unsigned int CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE = 256;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Macro: CHECK_CUDA\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Abort all MPI ranks if a CUDA runtime call fails\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                        \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,    \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                  \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                       \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: rootPrintf\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   printf restricted to MPI rank 0 so that output matches a serial run\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3))) static void rootPrintf(int rank, const char* fmt, ...) {\n    if (rank != 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n    va_list args;\n    va_start(args, fmt);\n    vprintf(fmt, args);\n    va_end(args);\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format on the host.\n//   Rows are independent; each row is summed sequentially, so the result is\n//   identical regardless of the number of OpenMP threads.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvCsrKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR SpMV on the device, one thread per row. The per-row accumulation order\n//   matches spmvCpu, so results agree with the reference implementation.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters: local CSR arrays (rowDelimiters rebased to 0)\n//   vec: dense input vector (full length)\n//   rows: number of local rows\n//   out: local output vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                              const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                              const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                              double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= rows) {\n        return;\n    }\n    double t = 0.0;\n    const index_t end = rowDelimiters[i + 1];\n    for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < end; ++j) {\n        t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n    }\n    out[i] = t;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: deviceAlloc / copyToDevice\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Allocate device memory (at least one element, so zero-row ranks are valid)\n//   and copy host vectors to it\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\ntemplate <typename T>\nT* deviceAlloc(size_t count) {\n    T* ptr = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&ptr), std::max<size_t>(count, 1) * sizeof(T)));\n    return ptr;\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid copyToDevice(T* dst, const std::vector<T>& src) {\n    if (!src.empty()) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dst, src.data(), src.size() * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(int rank, const char* progName) {\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Options:\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int numRanks = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &numRanks);\n\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(rank, argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            rootPrintf(rank, \"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(rank, argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", nItems,\n               100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Bind each rank to one GPU on its node\n    MPI_Comm nodeComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &nodeComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(nodeComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&nodeComm);\n\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Rank %d: no CUDA devices available\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaSetDevice(localRank % numDevices));\n\n    // Row partition balanced by non-zeros. rowStart has numRanks+1 entries;\n    // rank r owns rows [rowStart[r], rowStart[r+1]).\n    std::vector<index_t> rowStart(numRanks + 1);\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);\n    std::vector<double> l_val;\n    std::vector<index_t> l_cols;\n    std::vector<index_t> l_rowDelimiters;\n\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n    {\n        // Full matrix is generated on every rank with the same sequential RNG\n        // stream, so all ranks agree on the matrix without communication.\n        std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n        std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n        std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n\n        fill(h_vec.data(), numRows, maxVal);\n        fill(h_val.data(), nItems, maxVal);\n        initRandomMatrix(h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), nItems, numRows);\n\n        rowStart[0] = 0;\n        rowStart[numRanks] = numRows;\n        for (int r = 1; r < numRanks; ++r) {\n            const auto target = static_cast<index_t>((static_cast<uint64_t>(nItems) * r) / numRanks);\n            const auto it = std::lower_bound(h_rowDelimiters.begin(), h_rowDelimiters.end(), target);\n            rowStart[r] = std::min<index_t>(static_cast<index_t>(it - h_rowDelimiters.begin()), numRows);\n        }\n\n        // Extract this rank's CSR slice (OpenMP-parallel copy)\n        const index_t rowBegin = rowStart[rank];\n        const index_t rowEnd = rowStart[rank + 1];\n        const index_t localRows = rowEnd - rowBegin;\n        const index_t nnzBegin = h_rowDelimiters[rowBegin];\n        const index_t localNnz = h_rowDelimiters[rowEnd] - nnzBegin;\n\n        l_val.resize(localNnz);\n        l_cols.resize(localNnz);\n        l_rowDelimiters.resize(localRows + 1);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (index_t k = 0; k < localNnz; ++k) {\n            l_val[k] = h_val[nnzBegin + k];\n            l_cols[k] = h_cols[nnzBegin + k];\n        }\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (index_t i = 0; i <= localRows; ++i) {\n            l_rowDelimiters[i] = h_rowDelimiters[rowBegin + i] - nnzBegin;\n        }\n    }\n\n    const index_t localRows = rowStart[rank + 1] - rowStart[rank];\n    const index_t localNnz = static_cast<index_t>(l_val.size());\n\n    // Stage the local slice and the dense vector on the device\n    double* d_val = deviceAlloc<double>(localNnz);\n    index_t* d_cols = deviceAlloc<index_t>(localNnz);\n    index_t* d_rowDelimiters = deviceAlloc<index_t>(localRows + 1);\n    double* d_vec = deviceAlloc<double>(numRows);\n    double* d_out = deviceAlloc<double>(localRows);\n    copyToDevice(d_val, l_val);\n    copyToDevice(d_cols, l_cols);\n    copyToDevice(d_rowDelimiters, l_rowDelimiters);\n    copyToDevice(d_vec, h_vec);\n    // Zero the output so iterations == 0 yields the same zero vector as the original\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemset(d_out, 0, std::max<size_t>(localRows, 1) * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    // For validation, compute reference solution (rank-local rows, OpenMP on host)\n    std::vector<double> l_reference;\n    if (validate) {\n        rootPrintf(rank, \"Computing reference solution...\\n\");\n        l_reference.resize(localRows);\n        spmvCpu(l_val.data(), l_cols.data(), l_rowDelimiters.data(), h_vec.data(), localRows,\n                l_reference.data());\n    }\n\n    // Perform SpMV computation\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Computing SpMV...\\n\");\n    const auto numBlocks = static_cast<unsigned int>((localRows + CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE);\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    if (localRows > 0) {\n        for (index_t iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n            spmvCsrKernel<<<numBlocks, CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE>>>(d_val, d_cols, d_rowDelimiters, d_vec,\n                                                          localRows, d_out);\n        }\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", static_cast<long>(duration.count()));\n\n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    const double avgTime = duration.count() / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Retrieve local output and assemble the full vector on rank 0\n    std::vector<double> l_out(localRows);\n    if (localRows > 0) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(l_out.data(), d_out, localRows * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    }\n\n    std::vector<int> counts(numRanks);\n    std::vector<int> displs(numRanks);\n    for (int r = 0; r < numRanks; ++r) {\n        counts[r] = static_cast<int>(rowStart[r + 1] - rowStart[r]);\n        displs[r] = static_cast<int>(rowStart[r]);\n    }\n\n    std::vector<double> h_out(rank == 0 ? numRows : 0);\n    MPI_Gatherv(l_out.data(), static_cast<int>(localRows), MPI_DOUBLE, h_out.data(), counts.data(),\n                displs.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            print_results(h_out, \"OutputVector\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    int rc = 0;\n    if (validate) {\n        std::vector<double> h_reference(rank == 0 ? numRows : 0);\n        MPI_Gatherv(l_reference.data(), static_cast<int>(localRows), MPI_DOUBLE, h_reference.data(),\n                    counts.data(), displs.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        int valid = 0;\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            valid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), numRows) ? 1 : 0;\n            printf(valid ? \"Validation: PASSED\\n\" : \"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n        }\n        MPI_Bcast(&valid, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        rc = valid ? 0 : 1;\n    }\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(d_val));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(d_cols));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(d_rowDelimiters));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(d_vec));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(d_out));\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return rc;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793095789574,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"id":"prt_17cd652440013Cf3gJVHvj1LVp","messageID":"msg_17cd64d06001j4tF3bDUVMZFi1","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","type":"reasoning","text":"That's odd — CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES set to \"native\" resolved to compute_52 instead of the expected sm_86, likely because nvcc 12.0 failed to properly detect the RTX 3090's native architecture. It still works though, since the 3090 can run sm_52 code via PTX JIT.\n\nI should set explicit architectures instead of relying on \"native,\" since the cluster may have mixed GPUs. I'll go with a list like 70;80;86;90 to cover Volta through Hopper/Ada, which nvcc 12.0 supports, letting users override the default if needed.\n\nAlso interesting: the base build gives the same hash whether FMA contraction is on or off, suggesting the compiler isn't actually using FMA instructions here at all — maybe -march=native on this CPU doesn't enable them or vectorization isn't kicking in.\n\nBut CPU (9d9f) and GPU (ff73) results still diverge, which points to nvcc's default fmad=true behavior. I should test compiling with -fmad=false targeting sm_86 to confirm that's the source of the discrepancy.\n\n","time":{"start":1793095782980,"end":1793095789498},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793096666439,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"id":"prt_17ce34f9c001eQgHLds2yw0Vz3","messageID":"msg_17ce34a55001AXx3u0uRJ1fsnH","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","type":"reasoning","text":"Scaling looks good, so I want to verify correctness at this larger size by running validation with np 4 and comparing the hash against the base version. I'm also estimating theoretical bandwidth limits for the 3090—with nnz at 26.8M and 12 bytes per entry, ideal SpMV time should be around 0.35ms, but we're seeing 1.73ms, so there's room for improvement though current performance is reasonable.\n\nThe gap comes from uncoalesced row-per-thread access, but any optimization needs to preserve the exact sequential-per-row summation order for bit-identical results, which rules out warp-cooperative reordering. I'm considering whether a device-side preprocessing step could reorganize the sparse matrix into a warp-interleaved layout—grouping 32 rows per warp and storing their nonzeros in slot-major order with padding—to get better memory coalescing while still respecting the per-row accumulation order needed for exactness.\n\nSince row lengths follow a Poisson-ish distribution, naive padding across 32 rows would waste a lot of space, so sorting rows by length (SELL-C-sigma style) with an output permutation to restore order seems like the right fix—though I need to verify that padding zero entries doesn't quietly corrupt the floating-point result, especially around signed-zero edge cases.\n\nAn even cleaner alternative is to skip padding altogether: have each lane check its own row length against the current step and only accumulate when valid, which with sorted rows minimizes warp divergence and sidesteps the zero-padding correctness question entirely.\n\nGiven the current 62 GFLOPS baseline, a 3-5x kernel speedup seems worth pursuing despite the added complexity. The approach: sort local rows globally by length (descending) before assigning them to warps of 32, so each warp processes rows of similar length and divergence is minimized — sorting thousands of rows is cheap, and results get scattered back via the stored permutation.\n\nI'm working out the memory layout for packed warp data, figuring each warp's padding to its max row length is small overhead when sorted, so each warp's segment can be sized tightly to its own longest row rather than a global max.\n\nThe kernel then has each thread look up its sorted index's length and warp offset to accumulate the dot product and scatter results back using the permutation array, with lanes reading consecutive strided elements for coalesced access. Overhead per row is just 8 bytes for length and permutation index, so the storage cost stays minimal.\n\nThe output writes are scattered by the permutation but remain small per row, which should still be manageable, and since vec fits comfortably in L2 cache, random access there isn't a major bottleneck. Overall I estimate this restructuring could yield something like a 2-3x speedup over the naive uncoalesced per-row approach.\n\nThis seems worth implementing despite moderate complexity, especially since I have a strong hash-based validation check to catch bugs. On the host side, after slicing the local rows, I'll compute row lengths and build a permutation array sorting rows by length (descending so the longest row sets the warp's max length), using a stable sort over row indices — this setup cost happens once and isn't part of the timed kernel, so even for tens of millions of rows it should stay affordable.\n\nGrouping rows into warps of 32, each warp's slot count becomes 32 times its max row length, giving the total packed buffer size. Since the sort groups similar-length rows together, padding waste should stay small for roughly Poisson-distributed nonzero counts, and I only need to allocate memory for the padded slots without writing to the unused ones. Filling the packed array then iterates each sorted row, mapping it to its warp and lane, and writes its nonzero entries into the appropriate slots.\n\nThe kernel itself has each thread compute its warp base offset, then loop through its row's nonzero count reading packed values and columns at stride 32, accumulating the dot product in the original k-order to preserve numerical summation order, then scatter the result back to the unpermuted row index. Threads beyond the actual row count in the final partial warp simply don't execute, since the bounds check handles that safely.\n\nI'm also considering the memory overhead of this SELL-C-sigma layout: sorting rows by length keeps warps relatively uniform in practice, but worst-case pathological inputs (like one very long row grouped with many empty ones) could blow up padding to roughly 32x the true nonzero count for that warp, though this is bounded and rare with real sparse matrices.\n\nFor safety with very large matrices, I'll compute the total packed size in uint64 and guard against overflow of the 32-bit index type, fatally erroring if it would exceed UINT32_MAX. Then I need to write the host-side code that builds the sorted/packed array before copying to the device, alongside row lengths, permutation array, and warp pointer offsets.\n\nWriting packed CSR builder...\n\nI'm renaming the kernel from spmvCsrKernel, then moving to the host-side builder function that constructs the packed CSR structure, initializing the row permutation array and sorting rows by length.\n\nI'm sorting rows by descending length, computing per-row lengths after the permutation, and grouping rows into 32-wide slices where each slice's width is determined by its longest row (with overflow checks against UINT32_MAX) to build the slice offset table before allocating the value array.\n\nNow I'm parallelizing the scatter step: for each row, finding its slice and lane, then copying its values and column indices into the packed layout at strided positions. I'm also handling the empty-total edge case safely for device allocation and adding an overflow check that aborts with a rank-specific message if the packed size exceeds 32-bit range, before moving into staging the data for device transfer.\n\nIn main, I'm building the packed CSR structure from the local matrix data, then allocating device buffers sized from the packed vectors rather than the old nnz count, confirming the output gets written back in original row order via the permutation and that timing only covers the kernel itself. I'm keeping the packed host vectors scoped so they free after the device copy, and need to add the numeric header for iota before editing both the kernel and main sections.\n\n","time":{"start":1793096634268,"end":1793096666340},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793096676083,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_018LYMBCD45Bp3jQDDdHDMYG","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp","oldString":"// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvCsrKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR SpMV on the device, one thread per row. The per-row accumulation order\n//   matches spmvCpu, so results agree with the reference implementation.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters: local CSR arrays (rowDelimiters rebased to 0)\n//   vec: dense input vector (full length)\n//   rows: number of local rows\n//   out: local output vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                              const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                              const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                              double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= rows) {\n        return;\n    }\n    double t = 0.0;\n    const index_t end = rowDelimiters[i + 1];\n    for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < end; ++j) {\n        t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n    }\n    out[i] = t;\n}","newString":"// Rows per warp-sized slice of the packed device layout\nconstexpr index_t SLICE_HEIGHT = 32;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Struct: PackedCsr\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Device-friendly reordering of a CSR matrix slice. Rows are sorted by\n//   length (descending) so that the 32 rows of a warp have similar lengths.\n//   Within a slice, non-zeros are stored slot-major: element k of the lane-th\n//   row of slice w is at sliceOffset[w] + k*SLICE_HEIGHT + lane, so a warp reads\n//   consecutive memory on every step. Each row's non-zeros keep their original\n//   order, so per-row accumulation matches spmvCpu exactly.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nstruct PackedCsr {\n    std::vector<double> val;           // packed non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> cols;         // packed column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> sliceOffset;  // start of each slice (numSlices+1 entries)\n    std::vector<index_t> rowLen;       // non-zeros per row, indexed by sorted position\n    std::vector<index_t> rowPerm;      // original row index for each sorted position\n};\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: buildPackedCsr\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Builds the PackedCsr layout from CSR arrays (OpenMP-parallel packing)\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters: CSR arrays (rowDelimiters rebased to 0)\n//   rows: number of rows\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nPackedCsr buildPackedCsr(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n                         const index_t rows) {\n    PackedCsr p;\n    p.rowPerm.resize(rows);\n    for (index_t r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {\n        p.rowPerm[r] = r;\n    }\n    auto lenOf = [&](index_t r) { return rowDelimiters[r + 1] - rowDelimiters[r]; };\n    std::stable_sort(p.rowPerm.begin(), p.rowPerm.end(),\n                     [&](index_t a, index_t b) { return lenOf(a) > lenOf(b); });\n\n    p.rowLen.resize(rows);\n    for (index_t s = 0; s < rows; ++s) {\n        p.rowLen[s] = lenOf(p.rowPerm[s]);\n    }\n\n    // Slice offsets: each slice holds SLICE_HEIGHT * (longest row in slice) slots\n    const index_t numSlices = (rows + SLICE_HEIGHT - 1) / SLICE_HEIGHT;\n    p.sliceOffset.resize(numSlices + 1);\n    uint64_t total = 0;\n    p.sliceOffset[0] = 0;\n    for (index_t w = 0; w < numSlices; ++w) {\n        const uint64_t maxLen = p.rowLen[w * SLICE_HEIGHT];  // sorted: first row is longest\n        total += maxLen * SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        if (total > UINT32_MAX) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"Packed matrix slice exceeds 32-bit indexing\\n\");\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n        }\n        p.sliceOffset[w + 1] = static_cast<index_t>(total);\n    }\n\n    p.val.resize(total);\n    p.cols.resize(total);\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t s = 0; s < rows; ++s) {\n        const index_t w = s / SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        const index_t lane = s % SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        const index_t src = rowDelimiters[p.rowPerm[s]];\n        const index_t len = p.rowLen[s];\n        for (index_t k = 0; k < len; ++k) {\n            const index_t dst = p.sliceOffset[w] + k * SLICE_HEIGHT + lane;\n            p.val[dst] = val[src + k];\n            p.cols[dst] = cols[src + k];\n        }\n    }\n    return p;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvSlicedKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   SpMV on the device using the PackedCsr layout, one thread per row. Warps\n//   cover slices of length-sorted rows, so global loads are coalesced. Each row\n//   accumulates its non-zeros in the original order, matching spmvCpu.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, sliceOffset, rowLen, rowPerm: PackedCsr arrays\n//   vec: dense input vector (full length)\n//   rows: number of local rows\n//   out: local output vector, in original row order\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvSlicedKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                 const index_t* __restrict__ sliceOffset,\n                                 const index_t* __restrict__ rowLen,\n                                 const index_t* __restrict__ rowPerm,\n                                 const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                                 double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t s = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (s >= rows) {\n        return;\n    }\n    const index_t len = rowLen[s];\n    const index_t base = sliceOffset[s / SLICE_HEIGHT] + (s % SLICE_HEIGHT);\n    double t = 0.0;\n    for (index_t k = 0; k < len; ++k) {\n        const index_t idx = base + k * SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        t += val[idx] * vec[cols[idx]];\n    }\n    out[rowPerm[s]] = t;\n}"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp\n@@ -165,36 +165,123 @@\n         out[i] = t;\n     }\n }\n \n+// Rows per warp-sized slice of the packed device layout\n+constexpr index_t SLICE_HEIGHT = 32;\n+\n // ****************************************************************************\n-// Kernel: spmvCsrKernel\n+// Struct: PackedCsr\n //\n // Purpose:\n-//   CSR SpMV on the device, one thread per row. The per-row accumulation order\n-//   matches spmvCpu, so results agree with the reference implementation.\n+//   Device-friendly reordering of a CSR matrix slice. Rows are sorted by\n+//   length (descending) so that the 32 rows of a warp have similar lengths.\n+//   Within a slice, non-zeros are stored slot-major: element k of the lane-th\n+//   row of slice w is at sliceOffset[w] + k*SLICE_HEIGHT + lane, so a warp reads\n+//   consecutive memory on every step. Each row's non-zeros keep their original\n+//   order, so per-row accumulation matches spmvCpu exactly.\n //\n+// ****************************************************************************\n+struct PackedCsr {\n+    std::vector<double> val;           // packed non-zero values\n+    std::vector<index_t> cols;         // packed column indices\n+    std::vector<index_t> sliceOffset;  // start of each slice (numSlices+1 entries)\n+    std::vector<index_t> rowLen; Now I'm trying to figure out why the kernel is so slow at 436us for small per-GPU sizes, working through the math for np=4 with 4096 rows per rank and 1.68M nnz per rank to see what bandwidth that traffic should imply at 900GB/s.\n\nThat expected number comes out to roughly 22us, meaning the actual 436us is about 50x slower than expected, so something's clearly wrong in the kernel. I'm ruling out candidates one by one: the vec array size is fine at 128KB, the per-thread loop lengths look reasonable given the sorted order, and the launch configuration of 16 blocks by 256 threads seems unremarkable. The consistency across median and min runtimes rules out a first-launch warmup cost, and GPU clock ramp-up seems unlikely to explain it either, so I'm now focusing on the dependency chain within each thread's loop—each iteration requires sequential loads from global memory with DRAM latency around 400-600ns, and the compiler may not be pipelining these dependent loads across iterations, which could be the real bottleneck.\n\nWait, I realize I miscalculated the sparsity—with sparsity 10, each row actually has around 1638 nonzero entries, not 10, since nnz per row is n/10 for n=16384. That changes everything: each thread is doing roughly 1638 sequential dependent loads and FMAs per row, and even though the per-warp load pattern is coalesced across 32 lanes, with only 4096 threads total for np=4, there aren't nearly enough threads to hide that latency, which likely explains the slowdown.\n\nThis points to a fundamental tension: keeping bit-exact per-row sequential summation limits parallelism to one thread per row, which doesn't scale once rows get long and thread counts are low, whereas switching to a warp-per-row tree reduction would expose far more parallelism but sacrifice bit-identical results for an approximate tolerance.\n\nThe tolerance-based validation criterion in the benchmark actually permits this reassociation, so true scalability probably requires embracing warp/row splitting rather than clinging to strict ordering—though I'm also considering whether memory-level parallelism (prefetching loads ahead of the sequential add chain) could squeeze out gains while preserving exact ordering, even though the dependent adds themselves still form a long latency chain.\n\nWorking through the bandwidth math, unrolling loads by around 8 should let a bit-exact kernel saturate memory bandwidth reasonably well, bringing per-GPU time down from hundreds of microseconds to something closer to 40us, though I'm wary the compiler won't auto-unroll a dependent accumulation and I may need to manually stage loads into registers in chunks.\n\nWithout fast-math or FMA contraction flags, floating point adds won't get reordered, so strict sequential accumulation preserves bit-exactness. That leaves a real choice: stick with bit-exact chunked-load kernels that get decent but not maximal bandwidth, or go fully non-bit-exact with a warp-per-row scheme for best performance, relying on the tolerance-based validation since the original uses a 2% equivalence check that would tolerate floating-point reassociation.\n\nSince the -r mode output likely hashes results for exact external validation, I'm leaning toward keeping bit-exactness and squeezing performance through multi-level-parallelism via unrolled chunked loads rather than risking any reordering. Writing the unrolled chunk-loading kernel code...\n\nI'm thinking about whether software pipelining could help here—prefetching the next chunk's loads before accumulating the current one—but noting the compiler won't automatically hoist those loads above the accumulation step just from unrolling alone.\n\nI'll just go with UNROLL=8 as a baseline, measure it, and then try 16 as well. Multi-GPU threading and larger block sizes don't seem to offer further gains here, so I should just edit the kernel and test different UNROLL values directly.\n\n","time":{"start":1793097019735,"end":1793097039377},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

With thread-per-row, a 4-GPU split gives each GPU only 4096 threads, each running a long serial dependent load chain. That is latency-bound. More rows per GPU is not the fix, because the per-row sum must stay sequential to remain bit-identical.\n\nI can still hide latency without changing arithmetic order. With only 16 blocks in the grid, just 16 of the 82 SMs are active, each handling 8 warps.\n\nThis is the real bottleneck: occupancy is far too low to saturate memory bandwidth. With 16384 threads total spread across 82 SMs capable of 2048 threads each, occupancy sits around 0.2, way below what's needed for full bandwidth utilization. The in-flight bytes per thread with 8x unrolling should theoretically be enough (~96B per thread), yet measured bandwidth comes in at 430 GB/s for one config and only 235 GB/s for the 4-GPU case with 4096 threads, suggesting the in-flight data per thread isn't actually reaching the levels needed to hide memory latency.\n\nSomething besides raw occupancy is limiting things here — likely the dependency chain between loading indices and gathering values. If the compiler isn't prefetching the next chunk before finishing the FMA on the current chunk, each chunk pays the full round-trip latency, which checks out mathematically against the measured bandwidth numbers. The fix is either software pipelining to prefetch ahead, or simply increasing the unroll factor to keep more memory requests in flight simultaneously — I should try UNROLL=16 or 32 and see if that closes the gap, rebuilding and testing each variant.\n\n","time":{"start":1793097141973,"end":1793097149970},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793097493389,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"id":"prt_17cf01888001P10BFDfAVAc2oT","messageID":"msg_17cf01268001tq35ThAyNGJyHQ","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm checking the bandwidth math: single GPU handles the full 16384-row problem in 0.77ms, implying roughly 420GB/s throughput, while splitting across 4 GPUs at a quarter size each takes 0.32ms, giving only about 250GB/s per GPU—so the per-GPU efficiency actually drops with more GPUs.\n\nThe real culprit looks like occupancy: with only 4096 rows per GPU, that's just 128 warps spread across 82 SMs, barely 1-2 warps per SM, which is way too low to keep memory pipelines busy. Even the full 16384-row single-GPU case only gives about 6 warps per SM—still far below the roughly 32+ warps per SM needed to saturate the hardware, so this low thread count is likely the fundamental bottleneck across all configurations.\n\nSince FP addition isn't associative, maintaining bit-exact results forces a strictly sequential chain per row, meaning more parallelism within a row isn't an option without changing the output. I'm working out the latency math: with ~1638 sequential adds and loads in chunks, each thread needs roughly 205 chunk-loads, and if each takes about a microsecond, that alone explains the ~205us per-thread runtime — suggesting the fix has to come from exposing more concurrent loads per thread rather than restructuring the summation order.\n\nIncreasing unroll width doesn't cut the measured time, so something beyond raw latency is bottlenecking things — likely occupancy or per-SM memory pipeline limits rather than the dot-product itself. Given that, I'm leaning toward relaxing strict bitwise equivalence to reassociation-tolerant correctness, since the program's own validation is tolerance-based and the user explicitly wants maximum parallel performance and scalability — though this is a judgment call worth flagging.\n\nI'm now thinking through a warp-per-row CSR-vector scheme for the long rows (1638 nnz each): each warp strides lanes across a row's nonzeros for coalesced access and reduces via warp shuffle, giving good occupancy across thousands of resident warps.\n\nFor the benchmark's actual row lengths (~100 nnz at default settings), this warp-per-row approach is efficient and simple, though it would waste lanes on very sparse rows — acceptable given the target workload, and I'm deciding against adding a more complex adaptive/two-level scheme for now.\n\nRather than keeping the packed and sorted CSR variant, I'm simplifying back to the original CSR arrays directly for the device kernel, removing the extra packing step since it's unnecessary overhead. I'm now writing the warp-based SpMV kernel operating on these raw CSR arrays.\n\nWriting CUDA kernel code...\n\nI'm also thinking about launch configuration — mapping one warp per row, computing grid size with 256 threads per block (8 warps), and considering whether re-enabling FMA would help performance now that the packing/sorting approach is gone.\n\nSince CPU reference tests showed no difference between fused and non-fused multiply-add, and the kernel is memory-bound anyway, I'll drop the -fmad=false flag and just use the default CUDA fused-multiply-add semantics for simplicity and standard performance.\n\nI'm checking that warp-per-row reduction is deterministic and partition-independent across GPU counts, and confirming thread occupancy scales reasonably from n=1024 up through n=16384 and across multi-GPU row splits. Validation against the sequential OpenMP CPU reference should easily fall within the 2% relative tolerance despite tiny floating-point reassociation differences.\n\nI'm weighing bit-exactness versus speed: the exact-order path runs around 0.75ms on 4 GPUs while warp-per-row could hit roughly 0.05-0.1ms, a ~10x win, so I'll go with warp-per-row and clearly note that the output hash shifts in the last bits versus the original serial summation order even though validation still passes. The CPU reference stays sequential to preserve original semantics, and I'll keep rank-level row partitioning by nnz. Now I'm removing the PackedCsr structure and its builder function since they're no longer needed.\n\nNow I need to strip out the sliced kernel and constants, revert to plain CSR device arrays, update the kernel launch to use warp-per-row, and clean up the CMake flag — I'll make targeted edits to the file rather than rewriting it wholesale since most of it stays intact.\n\n","time":{"start":1793097472136,"end":1793097493331},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793097493390,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"id":"prt_17cf06b57001oxyCpkFS1PmgKp","messageID":"msg_17cf01268001tq35ThAyNGJyHQ","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","type":"text","text":"The single-GPU runs all take about 0.77 ms, and the 4-GPU case is only as fast as its slowest device. The real limit is occupancy: 16384 rows means only 16384 threads in total. Each GPU has 82 SMs, so even a 4-way split leaves each SM with only 1-2 warps. Per-row sequential summation cannot be parallelized further without changing the summation order.\n\nSo the trade-off is:\n- Keep bit-identical per-row summation, which caps scaling at about 0.7 ms per iteration regardless of GPU count.\n- Use a warp per row with a shuffle reduction, which gives enough parallelism and coalesced access. The result is reassociated within each row, so it differs in the last bits from the original. It stays deterministic and independent of rank count, and it is within the program's own 2% validation tolerance.\n\nSince you asked for maximum performance and scalability, I'll take the second option and state the change clearly. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793097526558,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01X8ZKHDCuTdpsoS16LGy4RB","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/spmv.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA sparse matrix-vector multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI: rows are partitioned across ranks, balanced by non-zero count.\n//          Each rank owns a contiguous block of CSR rows. The matrix is\n//          generated deterministically on every rank (identical to the serial\n//          generator), so no matrix data is communicated. The dense vector is\n//          constant across iterations, so the timed loop needs no communication.\n//   - CUDA: each rank drives one GPU (selected by node-local rank). A warp-per-row\n//          CSR kernel gives the GPU enough independent work to saturate memory\n//          bandwidth even when a rank holds few rows; lanes read consecutive\n//          non-zeros (coalesced) and reduce with warp shuffles.\n//   - OpenMP: host-side work that is data-parallel and rank-local: the CPU\n//          reference SpMV used for validation. The random matrix generator is\n//          inherently sequential (it consumes one rand() stream) and is kept\n//          serial so the generated matrix is identical to the original program.\n//\n// Numerics: each row is a sum of products. The GPU reduces each row's partial\n// sums in a fixed warp-tree order, which differs from the serial left-to-right\n// order only by floating-point reassociation. The result is deterministic and\n// independent of the number of ranks or GPUs, and is checked against the serial\n// reference with the same tolerance as before.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdarg>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\nconstexpr unsigned int WARP_SIZE = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned int CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE = 256;  // 8 warps per block\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Macro: CHECK_CUDA\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Abort all MPI ranks if a CUDA runtime call fails\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                        \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,    \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                  \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                       \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: rootPrintf\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   printf restricted to MPI rank 0 so that output is printed once\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3))) static void rootPrintf(int rank, const char* fmt, ...) {\n    if (rank != 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n    va_list args;\n    va_start(args, fmt);\n    vprintf(fmt, args);\n    va_end(args);\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format on the host.\n//   Rows are independent and each row is summed in order, so the result does\n//   not depend on the number of OpenMP threads.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvCsrVectorKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR SpMV on the device with one warp per row. Lanes stride over the row's\n//   non-zeros (coalesced loads), then combine partial sums with a warp shuffle\n//   reduction. Thread-per-row would leave most SMs idle when a rank holds few\n//   rows, because each row's sum is long.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters: local CSR arrays (rowDelimiters rebased to ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrVectorKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                    const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                                    const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                                    double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const uint64_t globalThread = static_cast<uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const uint64_t row = globalThread / WARP_SIZE;\n    if (row >= rows) {\n        return;  // whole warp exits together, so the shuffles below are safe\n    }\n    const unsigned int lane = threadIdx.x % WARP_SIZE;\n    const uint64_t end = rowDelimiters[row + 1];\n\n    double t = 0.0;\n    for (uint64_t j = rowDelimiters[row] + lane; j < end; j += WARP_SIZE) {\n        t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n    }\n\n    for (unsigned int offset = WARP_SIZE / 2; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n        t += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, t, offset);\n    }\n    if (lane == 0) {\n        out[row] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ptr = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&ptr), std::max<size_t>(count, 1) * sizeof(T)));\n    return ptr;\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid copyToDevice(T* dst, const std::vector<T>& src) {\n    if (!src.empty()) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dst, src.data(), src.size() * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n}\n\n// true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(int rank, const char* progName) {\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"Options:\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    rootPrintf(rank, \"  -i <num> {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793097787494,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"bash","callID":"toolu_0193PE8XUpJukyoz2CeRdvXw","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"command":"cat /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/CMakeLists.txt"},"output":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(spmv_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Required parallel runtimes: MPI (across ranks), OpenMP (host threads), CUDA (GPU)\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# Default to a fat binary covering common accelerator generations; override with\n# -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<list> to target a specific GPU model.\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 70 75 80 86 90)\nendif()\n\nadd_executable(spmv spmv.cpp)\n\n# The single source file contains CUDA kernels, so compile it with nvcc\nset_source_files_properties(spmv.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(spmv PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3;-march=native;-Wall;-Wextra;-fopenmp>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3;-Xcompiler=-march=native;-Xcompiler=-Wall;-Xcompiler=-Wextra;-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(spmv PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\ntarget_link_options(spmv PRIVATE -fopenmp)\n","metadata":{"output":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(spmv_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Required parallel runtimes: MPI (across ranks), OpenMP (host threads), CUDA (GPU)\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# Default to a fat binary covering common accelerator generations; override with\n# -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<list> to target a specific GPU model.\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 70 75 80 86 90)\nendif()\n\nadd_executable(spmv spmv.cpp)\n\n# The single source file contains CUDA kernels, so compile it with nvcc\nset_source_files_properties(spmv.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(spmv PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3;-march=native;-Wall;-Wextra;-fopenmp>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3;-Xcompiler=-march=native;-Xcompiler=-Wall;-Xcompiler=-Wextra;-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(spmv PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\ntarget_link_options(spmv PRIVATE -fopenmp)\n","exit":0,"truncated":false},"title":"cat /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/spmv/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793097787425,"end":1793097787456}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17cf4e80d001fFnsCIgLhYo6yI","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","messageID":"msg_17cf4c7b1001CjBLBguMkJx7mq"}}

{"type":"text","timestamp":1793097796143,"sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","part":{"id":"prt_17cf4f8cd001lo27pOr5KTHyZ3","messageID":"msg_17cf4f220001ZH1fVkHLV31Yxm","sessionID":"ses_e832e179dffe1JpmdauGHjm2Hu","type":"text","text":"The SpMV benchmark now runs as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. Only `spmv/spmv.cpp` and `spmv/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable is still `spmv`, and no files were added.\n\n**Results are not bit-identical to the original.** The original summed each row strictly left to right. The GPU kernel uses a warp-level tree reduction per row, so the last bits differ. The `-r` hash therefore changes (for example, `20c6ca8034bcb7cd` in the original becomes `0426e8f0b4334b41` for n=4096). The deviation is about 1e-15 relative, `-v` passes, and the result is identical across rank counts. If you need the original hash, tell me and I'll switch to a sequential per-row kernel, which caps scaling at roughly one GPU's throughput.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** Rows are split across ranks, balanced by nonzero count. Every rank regenerates the matrix with the same serial RNG, so no matrix data is communicated. The vector is constant across iterations, so the timed loop has no communication. Rank 0 gathers the output for printing and validation.\n- **CUDA:** Each rank binds to one GPU by node-local rank. A warp-per-row CSR kernel gives enough parallelism to saturate memory bandwidth on a few rows per GPU. The earlier thread-per-row version was occupancy-limited and did not scale across GPUs.\n- **OpenMP:** Used for the rank-local CSR slicing and the CPU reference SpMV used by `-v`. The RNG-driven matrix generator stays serial because it consumes a single `rand()` stream.\n- **CMake:** Requires CMake 3.24 (raised from 3.10), MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA. The default CUDA architectures are 70, 75, 80, 86, and 90, and can be overridden with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. The GPU is required at runtime, as you asked.\n\n**Verification**\n- Built with no warnings. Validation passes for ranks 1, 2, 3, 4, and 8 (8 oversubscribed on 4 GPUs), across several matrix sizes and edge cases (1 row, 0 iterations, fewer rows than ranks).\n- Help and unknown-option paths behave as before.\n\n**Performance** (n=16384, s=10, 1000 iterations, RTX 3090s):\n\n| Config | Time per iteration | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original serial | 41.6 ms | 1.3 |\n| 1 GPU | 0.39 ms | 137 |\n| 2 GPUs | 0.20 ms | 264 |\n| 4 GPUs | 0.11 ms | 484 |\n\nPer-GPU bandwidth is about 825 GB/s, close to the card's peak. Timing excludes matrix generation and host/device copies, as the original excluded setup.\n\n**Caveats**\n- I ran only on a single 4-GPU node, so multi-node behavior is untested.\n- Matrix generation is still serial and is repeated on every rank, which may dominate startup for very large `-n`. It is outside the timed region.","time":{"start":1793097791693,"end":1793097796140}}}
